KEY MESSAGE 1...

Current KENX radar already shows some light showers approaching the 
southern areas before overspreading the rest of the region by 
evening. The 990 mb cyclone tracking north will approach the Mid-
Atlantic Region before lifting through tomorrow. The strong low 
along with the negatively tilted parent trough will result in strong 
forcing for ascent allowing for a 6-10 hour period of rain. With 
strong easterly/southeasterly flow, significant moisture advection 
from the Gulf has increased PWATs to 1-1.5" about +2 to +3 STDEV 
above normal and above the climatological 90th percentile. Rain will 
be moderate to heavy at times with max rainfall rates reaching 0.5" 
for brief periods , especially in the evening to first half of the 
overnight hours (about 01 UTC to 05 UTC) which could result in 
difficult and/or slowed holiday travel. Total QPF remains similar to 
the previous forecast ranging from 0.5" to 1.5", although locally 
higher amounts may occur in areas of higher terrain from 
upslope/downslope factors. Probabilities for > 2.00" of rain are 40-
80% for limited areas where upslope is favored in northwest CT and 
eastern Catskills. Given dry antecedent conditions and lack of rain 
for the past two weeks, flooding is not anticipated although ponding 
of water may occur especially in urban and poor drainage locations. 
Minor tidal flooding is also expected along the Hudson River at 
Poughkeepsie during the high tidal cycles this afternoon through 
tomorrow morning.  The rain should taper off to showers overnight 
into the pre-dawn hours tomorrow, as a dry slot moves in from the 
south. Additional showers are expected throughout the day tomorrow, 
as the main core of the upper low gradually moves in from the 
south/west. 

The Winter Weather Advisory remains unchanged for parts of the S. 
Adirondacks and S. Greens for some light icing due to freezing rain 
in sheltered areas there. Still expecting surface temperatures to be 
near 32F at precipitation onset and for a few hours after 
through the evening, with a pronounced layer of warm air aloft 
developing. Isolated spots in the eastern Catskills could also 
see a brief period of freezing rain initially, but should 
quickly turn over to plain rain. Where the freezing rain 
occurs, radial ice accumulation in these limited areas should
only be a few hundredths to < 0.10". Freezing rain will change 
to plain rain overnight as surface temperatures warm.

KEY MESSAGE 2...

The strong cyclone and parent trough tracking inland and anticylone 
to our north, pressure gradients continue to strengthen allowing for 
strong gusts across the region today into tonight. With the latest hi-
res models showing wind gusts up to 60 mph in parts of eastern New 
York and western New England and in collaboration with neighboring 
offices, the Wind Advisory for northern Berkshire, eastern 
Rensselaer, and Bennington Counties has been upgraded to a High Wind 
Warning through tomorrow morning. The Wind Advisory remains in 
effect for southern Herkimer County, the eastern Catskills, western 
Mohawk Valley, and Litchfield County. As the storm system 
approaches, ensemble models show an anomalous high easterly (u 
component) 850 mb LLJ, -4 to -5 STDEV, at a 60-80 kt developing 
overhead this evening. Being in the warm sector of the low, a 
notable inversion exists which could act to limit momentum transfer 
from the LLJ, but forecast soundings show a pocket of stronger 40 kt 
wind displaced just beneath the inversion at about 2,000 ft AGL 
which will, along with enhanced channeling and downsloping in high 
terrain areas, still mix down impactful wind gusts at the surface. 
The strongest wind gusts (up to 60 mph) are expected in the High 
Wind Warning areas within the 22 UTC to 05 UTC timeframe peaking 
around 03 UTC when breaks in the rain begin. There are increased 
probabilities of 40-50 mph gusts in Wind Advisory areas. Gusts of 25-
40 mph will be common elsewhere. Strong winds will blow around 
unsecured outdoors objects and blow down tree limbs. Power outages 
may result. Winds will gradually weaken after about 05 UTC into 
tomorrow morning as the LLJ shifts north of the area.

KEY MESSAGE 3...

From previous discussion: 

The next system approaching from the west, looks to bring another 
round of mainly rain Sun night into Mon. Guidance showing a 
progressive trough aloft, with a surface cyclone passing by 
north/west of our area, with a trailing cold front moving east 
across the region. Due to quick movement and relatively limited 
moisture, rainfall amounts will be less than today's system. NBM 
probabilities for > 0.50" rain are only 20-70%, with the highest 
chances in favored upslope areas of the SW. Adirondacks and S. 
Greens. Temperatures should be mild enough for plain rain, except 
for some brief snow showers in parts of the Adirondacks later Mon as 
colder air may briefly filter in prior to precip ending.
